learn.purpose: Collect representative evidence and compile an unapproved candidate.

audit.purpose: Evaluate one exact candidate artifact set without activating candidate denies.

enforce.purpose: Run only an approved, image-bound profile and deny behavior outside it.

egress-learn.purpose: Collect scoped outbound network evidence for one workspace and image.

egress-audit.purpose: Evaluate one exact scoped egress candidate while recording would-deny traffic.

egress-enforce.purpose: Apply an approved workspace- and image-bound outbound allowlist without claiming ingress enforcement.

notes: Learn and audit load no compiler-generated Tetragon policy; built-in lifecycle events and separately authored monitor sensors provide evidence.
An enforcement-capable Tetragon policy may be activated only from an approved profile directory after the daemon verifies every approval hash.

The current audit runtime records exact candidate hashes but marks Tetragon, seccomp, AppArmor, Docker, and full network evaluation incomplete; those runs are evidence-bearing but cannot satisfy promotion.

The shipped standalone supervisor rejects enforce admission because its managed gateway enforces egress but does not evaluate the compiled ingress policy; use an external manager only after it supplies and attests that missing backend.
Scoped egress modes never load candidate seccomp, AppArmor, Tetragon, Docker, or ingress artifacts; the baseline runner hardening remains active.

egress-enforce releases a runner only after the daemon snapshots the verified scoped approval and nosh-egress attests the exact cgroup, run, image, workspace, policy digest, pinned maps, links, and programs.
egress-audit and egress-enforce evidence is diagnostic-only and cannot train a wider replacement allowlist.
Legacy local net approve records are historical review receipts and never authorize egress-enforce; only the current root-owned signed guard-ebpf activation can do so.
Scoped egress uses an ordinary per-run Docker bridge for routing and NAT; nosh-egress is the sole scoped allow/deny decision point.
egress-learn DNS and L4 decisions are emitted by one eBPF backend; loss, truncation, parser errors, map exhaustion, and ambiguous correlations invalidate candidate promotion.
